title: SLO Sentry Snooze and Safe-Reopen Stabilizer
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduce conditional SLO snooze window and circuit reopen backoff to reduce flapping and spurious SLO incidents. Includes telemetry annotations and a controlled rollout toggle.
description: Context: During a recent cross-region flapping event we observed repeated circuit reopen attempts that caused SLO enforcement to oscillate and produced noisy customer impact metrics. The control plane and serving runtime reacted too quickly, triggering widespread soft-degradation and hampering recovery. Motivation: Reduce oscillation between enforcement and reopen by introducing a short, conditional "snooze" period where SLO enforcement is relaxed for affected tenants/cohorts, and add a safe-reopen stabilizer that enforces exponential reopen backoff and a bounded 'probe' window. Design summary: 1) SLO Sentry Snooze: a control-plane policy that detects a short-lived spike in error/latency signals for a tenant or region and sets a temporary SLO-snooze flag (configurable 30s-5m). While snoozed, routing uses a prioritized, probationary slowpath with limited token allotment rather than immediate circuit demotion. 2) Safe-Reopen Stabilizer: runtime-level coordinator that records reopen attempts per circuit and enforces exponential backoff with jitter, plus an optional probe token (single request) to validate readiness before fully reopening. 3) KV Evacuation Safety Net: when a node transitions to draining due to a snooze window, we snapshot and extend KV TTLs by a short margin to prevent cache loss during rapid drain/rejoin cycles. 4) Telemetry & Audit: annotate SLO events with snooze_reason and reopen_backoff metadata, emit metrics for snooze_count, probe_success, and kv_snapshot_hits. 5) Feature flag & rollout: implemented behind a feature flag (slo_sentry_snooze) and controlled server-side config with safe defaults. Checklist: - Implement control-plane policy + unit tests - Add runtime coordinator and backoff logic - Telemetry annotations & Grafana panels - E2E chaos test for reopen flapping - Documentation and runbook updates - Add feature flag and migration script Why this is safe: The change is opt-in via feature flag; default snooze window is conservative (30s). Probe semantics ensure at least one request validates readiness before mass reopen. KV TTL extension window is short and bounded to avoid resource leak. Migration: No DB schema changes. A small config addition to the control plane (feature flag + default snooze policy) — rollout plan below. Rollout plan: 1) Canary: enable for 5% of tenants in us-west and eu-central for 24 hours with increased telemetry retention. 2) Observe snooze_count and probe_success. If probe_success > 90% and no unintended increase in latency, expand to 30% traffic. 3) Full enable with monitoring dashboards and auto rollback on SLI degradation. Testing performed: - Unit tests for backoff math and snooze TTLs - Integration test simulating reopen flapping with mocked KV store - E2E in benchmark-lab with controlled failure window - Manual operator dry-run on staging with real production traffic clones Commits summary: - feat(sentry): add control-plane SLO snooze policy and config (Asha Patel) - feat(runtime): implement reopen stabilizer and backoff coordinator with probe token (Asha Patel) - perf(kv): safe snapshot TTL extension and drain marker (Miguel Torres) - telemetry: add snooze annotations and metrics, update dashboards (Priya Nair) - docs: RFC and runbook + rollout checklist (Liam Chen) Changed files (high level): - controlplane/policies/slo_sentry.go - runtime/circuit/reopen_stabilizer.go - runtime/circuit/snooze_manager.go - runtime/kv/snapshotter.go - telemetry/annotations.go - dashboards/grafana/slo_sentry_overview.json - docs/rfc/slo-sentry-snooze.md - tests/unit/snooze_manager_test.go Review thread summary: - Miguel Torres: "Main concern is ensuring we don't hide real regressions with snooze. Can we limit snooze to non-critical tenants initially?" Author reply: "Yes — policy supports tenant cohorts and service-level gating; rollout will target low-risk tenants first." - Priya Nair: "Please add histogram buckets for probe latency and annotate spans so we can trace probe->open sequences." Author reply: "Added probe histogram and span annotation in telemetry patch." - Liam Chen: "Two nits on naming and one potential race in snapshot TTL update." Requested change: add a TTL update mutex in snapshotter. Author updated commit to introduce a lightweight mutex and added unit test covering racing drains. - SRE (Miguel) approved after change. - Product (Priya) gave final OK for experimental rollout. CI & validations: - CI pipeline: unit / integration / lint - Initial CI run: lint failed on naming convention; fixed in commit 3 - Second run: flakey integration test (kv_snapshot_integration) failed; re-ran, passed - Final status: all checks passing (unit, integration, e2e smoke) Merge outcome: Squash-merged by Liam Chen after approvals and a successful canary dry-run in staging Notes for on-call: If SLO snooze causes unexpected masking of customer errors, toggle slo_sentry_snooze off via control-plane flag and revert reopen backoff via runtime override. Runbook: docs/runbooks/slo-sentry-snooze-runbook.md (added) Related work: ENG-1987 (incident follow-up), ENG-2045 (kv-evacuation improvements).
